newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMPLATS PROFITS SEEN UP ON VOLUME,COST CUTS.
newsitem.headline: IMPLATS PROFITS SEEN UP ON VOLUME,COST CUTS.

text.p: Rising volumes and rigid cost control are expected to raise full year profits for South Africa's second largest platinum producer Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats), analysts said on Friday.

"Unlike last year they haven't had too much industrial unrest. A weaker rand and higher production will all contribute and I think they've also been controlling their unit costs better," said BOE Natwest platinum analyst Paul Brogan.

The group, which reports on Thursday, was forecast to chalk up earnings per share of 322 cents for the year to June 30 from 282 cents a year ago. Its total year dividend was seen rising to 123 cents from 100 cents.
Analysts' earnings forecasts ranged between 311-339 cents while dividends were called between 110-135 cents.
Implats has been in recovery since its woeful 1997/97 results, which saw earnings crushed by more than a third on lost output, capital costs and miscalculated currency hedges.
First half earnings per share for 1996/97 nudged 3.3 percent higher despite a loss of 100 million rand stemming from accumulated forward cover losses.
Analysts said there would be no forward cover-related hit on the second half bottom line.
They said Implats would have benefitted from the rand's weakness over fiscal 1996/97 which had more than offset the white metal's spot market weakness.

Spot platinum prices averaged $385.42 an ounce for the 52 weeks to June 30, from an average of $413.61 for the same period a year earlier. At the same time, the rand averaged 4.5237 to the dollar from 3.8468 a year ago.
Analysts said the company had also reigned in costs, particularly at the refinery stage, as well as enjoying steadier contract refining business.

"The refineries are going to come through in the half. I don't think there'll be anything spectacular from the mines," said one analyst who expected earnings per share of 311 cents but said the result might be as high as 335 cents
"Cost savings will be driven at the refinery level. They have good controls and they do toll refining as well, the profits from which will offset some costs."
Some analysts were punting on Implats' platinum output cracking one million ounces from 972,000 ounces a year earlier.
Huysamer Stals platinum analyst Errol Keller said output would be assisted by the destocking of the refinery pipeline after last year's leakage at the No 5 furnace.
The furnace -- which accounts for about 80 percent of total output -- had to be shut last August and then operated below full production for almost three months while repairs were made.
